title: Smooth commutative p-torsion affine groups embed into an additive group power
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic $p>0$. Let $H$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] commutative affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $[p]_H=0$: for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, the sum of $p$ copies of every element of $H(R)$ is zero. Then there exist $n\geq0$ and a homomorphism $i:H\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_a^n$ of $k$-group schemes identifying $H$ with a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Here $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ [def-sc-gm-ga], its power has coordinatewise addition, and $\mathbf G_a^0=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with its trivial group law. Neither connectedness of $H$ nor perfection of $k$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 14.49, printed p.296, with the definition of elementary unipotent in Definition 14.45, printed p.295. Proposition 14.49 uses Proposition 14.48 and 11.41.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-verschiebung] to $H$, writing $C=k[H]$, $C^{(p)}=C\otimes_{k,\sigma}k$, $f_C=F_H^*$ and $v_C=V_H^*$, with $\sigma(c)=c^p$. Its hypotheses are exactly affineness, finite type, commutativity and characteristic $p$. Smoothness of $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ implies that its only fibre $H$ is geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Since $\sigma:k\to k$ is a field embedding, the base change $\operatorname{Spec}C^{(p)}$ is reduced; in particular $C^{(p)}$ has no nonzero nilpotents, by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. For $z=\sum a_i\otimes c_i$, the formula for $f_C$ gives $f_C(z)\otimes1=\sum c_i a_i^p\otimes1=\sum a_i^p\otimes c_i^p=z^p$. Thus $f_C(z)=0$ implies $z^p=0$ and then $z=0$; this proves injectivity without assuming connectedness or perfection.

source.place: Proposition 14.49, printed p.296, using 11.40(a), 11.41, 14.48 and the coordinate formulation of 14.45.

proof.text: The assumption on all algebra-valued points says $[p]_H$ is the constant identity morphism: evaluate it at the universal point on the affine scheme $H$. The identity $V_H\circ F_H=[p]_H$ of [lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-verschiebung] therefore yields $f_Cv_C(a)=\epsilon(a)1_C$ for every $a\in C$. Also $f_C(\epsilon(a)1_{C^{(p)}})=\epsilon(a)1_C$. Injectivity from step 1 gives $v_C(a)=\epsilon(a)1_{C^{(p)}}$. Consequently $V_H$ is the zero group homomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 14.49, printed p.296, using 11.40(a), 11.41, 14.48 and the coordinate formulation of 14.45.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-zero-verschiebung-primitive-generation] with $G=H$ and the zero Verschiebung established in step 2: $C$ is generated by primitive elements. Independently, [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra] applies to the given affine finite-type $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $C$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra. In the explicit sense of [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], choose algebra generators $c_1,\ldots,c_m$ of $C$.

source.place: Proposition 14.49, printed p.296, using 11.40(a), 11.41, 14.48 and the coordinate formulation of 14.45.

proof.text: For each $c_j$, primitive generation gives an expression as a polynomial in finitely many primitive elements. Take the finite union of the elements occurring in these $m$ expressions and enumerate it as $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. The $k$-subalgebra they generate contains every $c_j$, hence is all of $C$. Therefore the evaluation map $q:k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to C$, $t_i\mapsto x_i$, is surjective. The union may be empty: then $C=k$ and $n=0$.

source.place: Proposition 14.49, printed p.296, using 11.40(a), 11.41, 14.48 and the coordinate formulation of 14.45.

proof.text: The coordinate Hopf maps of $H$ are supplied by [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. For each primitive $x_i$, applying $\epsilon\otimes1$ to $\Delta(x_i)=x_i\otimes1+1\otimes x_i$ gives $\epsilon(x_i)=0$. The antipode identity then gives $S(x_i)+x_i=0$. Thus the map $q$ of step 4 respects coproduct, counit and antipode: on each $t_i$ these are $t_i\otimes1+1\otimes t_i$, $0$, and $-t_i$ for the coordinatewise additive group [def-sc-gm-ga]. By [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor], $i=\operatorname{Spec}q:H\to\mathbf G_a^n$ is a group-scheme homomorphism. Both schemes are affine and $q$ is surjective, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](2), with the single affine target chart, makes $i$ a closed immersion. This identifies $H$ with a closed subgroup as defined in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]: its image is a subgroup on each algebra-valued point because $i$ is an injective homomorphism. When $n=0$, $q:k\to C=k$ is an isomorphism and this is the identity embedding of the trivial group.
